questions.question: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease is characterised by:

options.D: Atrophy of the peroneal muscles (peroneal muscular atrophy)

questions.explanation: CMT is a hereditary motor and sensory neuropathy causing distal wasting and a high-arched foot.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The area responsible for the motor aspect of speech is:
questions.explanation: Broca's area (inferior frontal gyrus) controls speech production.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The area responsible for the sensory aspect (comprehension) of speech is:
questions.explanation: Wernicke's area (posterior superior temporal gyrus) handles speech comprehension.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Language, logic and analytical problem solving are mainly functions of the:
questions.explanation: In most people the left hemisphere is dominant for language and analytical thinking.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Spatial relationships, artistic ability and body image awareness are mainly functions of the:
questions.explanation: The right hemisphere handles visuospatial skills, art and body awareness.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Executive functions (planning and judgement) are the main function of the ______ lobe.
questions.explanation: The frontal lobe, particularly the prefrontal cortex, handles executive functions.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Spatial and visual perception is mainly a function of the ______ lobe.
questions.explanation: The parietal lobe integrates sensory information and spatial awareness.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The primary auditory processing centre lies in the ______ lobe.
questions.explanation: The temporal lobe contains Heschl's gyrus (auditory cortex).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The primary visual processing centre lies in the ______ lobe.
questions.explanation: The primary visual cortex lies around the calcarine sulcus.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Agnosia and apraxia are most typical of damage to the ______ lobe.
questions.explanation: Parietal lesions produce perceptual disorders such as agnosia and apraxia.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Homonymous hemianopia is typical of damage to the ______ lobe or the optic radiations.
questions.explanation: Occipital lesions cause contralateral homonymous field loss.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The hippocampus is mainly concerned with:
questions.explanation: The hippocampus acts as a memory indexer, converting short-term to long-term memory.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The thalamus functions mainly as a:
questions.explanation: Almost all sensory pathways synapse in the thalamus before reaching the cortex.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The epithalamus (pineal gland) is concerned with:
questions.explanation: The pineal gland secretes melatonin, regulating sleep-wake cycles.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Commissural fibres:

options.A: Connect the cortex to the spinal cord
options.B: Connect the cerebellum to the pons
options.D: Connect different parts within the same hemisphere

questions.explanation: The corpus callosum is the main commissural pathway.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Projection fibres:

options.A: Connect different areas within a hemisphere
options.C: Connect the cortex to the spinal cord and other brain parts

questions.explanation: The internal capsule contains projection fibres.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Association fibres:

options.A: Connect the cortex to the spinal cord
options.B: Connect different parts within the same hemisphere
options.D: Connect the spinal nerves to muscles

questions.explanation: Examples are the arcuate fasciculus and cingulum.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The ______ (neocerebellum) is responsible for fine, skilled movements.
questions.explanation: The neocerebellum (pontocerebellum, lateral hemispheres) coordinates skilled voluntary movement.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Maintenance of equilibrium is the function of the:
questions.explanation: The flocculonodular lobe (archicerebellum) connects with the vestibular nuclei.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The paleocerebellum (spinocerebellum) is responsible for:

options.C: Synergistic control of muscle tone and posture

questions.explanation: The anterior lobe/vermis regulates muscle tone, gait and posture.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Dysdiadochokinesia, dysmetria and dyssynergia are signs of a lesion of the:
questions.explanation: Hemispheric lesions cause ipsilateral limb incoordination.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A truncal ataxia with disturbed vestibulo-ocular reflexes suggests a lesion of the:
questions.explanation: The vestibulocerebellum controls balance and eye movements.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The anterior cerebral artery supplies the:

options.B: Occipital lobe and inferior temporal lobe

questions.explanation: The ACA supplies the anterior and medial parts of the frontal lobe and medial parietal lobe (leg area).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The posterior cerebral artery supplies the:

options.C: Occipital lobe and inferior temporal lobe

questions.explanation: The PCA supplies the visual cortex and inferior surface of the temporal lobe.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The vertebrobasilar system supplies the:
questions.explanation: The basilar and vertebral arteries supply the brainstem and cerebellum.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following cranial nerves is purely sensory?
questions.explanation: Pure sensory nerves are I, II and VIII.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following cranial nerves is purely motor?
questions.explanation: Pure motor cranial nerves are III, IV, VI, XI and XII.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following cranial nerves is a mixed nerve?
questions.explanation: Mixed cranial nerves are V, VII, IX and X.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which cranial nerve moves the eye upward, downward and inward?
questions.explanation: The oculomotor nerve supplies superior, inferior and medial rectus and inferior oblique.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which cranial nerve moves the adducted eye downward?
questions.explanation: The trochlear nerve supplies superior oblique, which depresses the adducted eye.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which cranial nerve abducts the eye (moves it outward)?
questions.explanation: The abducens nerve supplies lateral rectus.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In Weber's test, if there is conductive hearing loss in one ear the sound will be lateralised to the:
questions.explanation: In conductive loss the affected ear hears the fork louder because of reduced masking.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In Weber's test, in sensorineural hearing loss the sound is heard louder in the:
questions.explanation: Sensorineural loss lateralises the sound to the better ear.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In Rinne's test, conductive hearing loss is shown when:

options.B: Air conduction is greater than bone conduction
options.D: Bone conduction is greater than air conduction

questions.explanation: A negative Rinne (BC > AC) indicates conductive loss.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In Rinne's test, sensorineural hearing loss gives:

options.B: Air conduction greater than bone conduction (positive Rinne)
options.C: Bone conduction greater than air conduction

questions.explanation: In sensorineural loss the normal pattern AC > BC is preserved.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The vestibulocochlear nerve is commonly tested with a tuning fork of:
questions.explanation: A 512 Hz tuning fork is used for Rinne and Weber tests.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In paralysis of the glossopharyngeal nerve, sensation (and taste) is lost from the ______ of the tongue.
questions.explanation: The glossopharyngeal nerve supplies the posterior third of the tongue.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In an injury of the hypoglossal (12th) nerve, the tongue on protrusion deviates to the ______ side.
questions.explanation: Genioglossus on the intact side pushes the tongue toward the weak (injured) side.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A state from which the patient cannot be aroused and remains unconscious is:
questions.explanation: Coma is unarousable unresponsiveness.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A state from which the patient can be aroused only by a painful stimulus is:
questions.explanation: Stupor responds only to vigorous or painful stimulation.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A state in which the patient is conscious but has reduced alertness, slow response and reduced interest in the environment is:
questions.explanation: Obtundation is mild-to-moderate reduction in alertness.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A Glasgow Coma Scale of 13-15 indicates a ______ brain injury.
questions.explanation: GCS 13-15 mild, 9-12 moderate, 3-8 severe.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A Glasgow Coma Scale of 9-12 indicates a ______ brain injury.
questions.explanation: GCS 9-12 is a moderate head injury.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A Glasgow Coma Scale of 8 or less indicates a ______ brain injury.
questions.explanation: GCS 3-8 is severe and usually requires airway protection.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: According to the Rancho Los Amigos scale, level 1 signifies:
questions.explanation: Level I is no response to any stimulus.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: According to the Rancho Los Amigos scale, levels 4, 5 and 6 signify:
questions.explanation: Level IV confused-agitated, V confused-inappropriate, VI confused-appropriate.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: According to the Rancho Los Amigos scale, levels 2 and 3 signify:
questions.explanation: Level II generalised and level III localised response.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which aphasia is fluent but with impaired language comprehension?
questions.explanation: Wernicke's aphasia is fluent with poor comprehension.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In Kernig's sign the patient lies supine, the hip and knee are flexed, and the examiner then:

options.A: Extends the knee, which causes pain or resistance in meningeal irritation
options.C: Flexes the neck onto the chest

questions.explanation: Kernig's sign tests hamstring resistance to knee extension with the hip flexed.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In Brudzinski's neck sign the examiner flexes the neck to the chest in supine and a positive response is:

options.C: Involuntary flexion of the hips and knees

questions.explanation: Flexion of the neck produces reflex flexion of the lower limbs in meningeal irritation.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a superficial sensation?
questions.explanation: Joint position sense is a deep sensation.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a deep sensation?
questions.explanation: Barognosis (weight discrimination) is a cortical sensation, not a deep one.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is a cortical (combined) sensation?
questions.explanation: Cortical sensations include stereognosis, graphaesthesia, barognosis, two-point and tactile localisation.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Vibration sense is commonly tested with a tuning fork of:
questions.explanation: A 128 Hz tuning fork on a bony prominence tests vibration; 512 Hz is for hearing.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A Modified Ashworth grade of 3 indicates:

options.A: Rigid limb in flexion or extension
options.B: Considerable increase in tone; passive movement is difficult
options.C: Marked increase in tone but limb easily moved
options.D: Slight increase with catch and release

questions.explanation: MAS 3: considerable increase in tone throughout the range with difficult passive movement.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A Modified Ashworth grade of 1 indicates a slight increase in tone with:

options.C: Resistance through most of the range
options.D: A catch and release or minimal resistance at the end of the range

questions.explanation: MAS 1: slight increase in tone, a catch and release or minimal resistance at the end of ROM.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is velocity-dependent?
questions.explanation: Spasticity increases with the speed of passive stretch; rigidity does not.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Muscle tone is normal or reduced in lesions of the:
questions.explanation: Cerebellar lesions cause hypotonia or normal tone, unlike basal ganglia (rigidity) or pyramidal lesions (spasticity).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Sensation is typically preserved in lesions of the:
questions.explanation: Basal ganglia and cerebellar lesions cause motor disturbance without sensory loss.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The gait seen in a cerebellar lesion is:
questions.explanation: Cerebellar disease produces a wide-based, staggering ataxic gait.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: When the increase in tone is encountered uniformly throughout the range of motion, the rigidity is called:
questions.explanation: Lead-pipe rigidity is a constant resistance throughout movement, as in Parkinson's disease.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: When the increase in tone is encountered in a series of jerks (catches) as the limb is moved through its range, the rigidity is called:
questions.explanation: Cogwheel rigidity is lead-pipe rigidity with superimposed tremor.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In decerebrate rigidity:

options.A: Limbs and trunk are in flexion
options.B: Upper and lower limbs and the trunk are in extension
options.C: Upper limbs are extended and lower limbs are flexed
options.D: Upper limbs are flexed and lower limbs are extended

questions.explanation: Decerebrate posturing (brainstem lesion below the red nucleus) shows extension of all limbs with arching of the back.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In decorticate rigidity:

options.A: Limbs and trunk are in flexion
options.B: Upper limbs are extended and lower limbs flexed
options.C: Upper and lower limbs are extended
options.D: Upper limbs are flexed and lower limbs are extended

questions.explanation: Decorticate posturing (lesion above the red nucleus) shows arms flexed on the chest and legs extended.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In opisthotonos:

options.B: The limbs are flexed and adducted
options.C: Only the upper limbs are extended
options.D: The head, neck and spine arch backward in extension

questions.explanation: Opisthotonos is severe hyperextension of the back, seen in tetanus and meningitis.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The cremasteric reflex is mediated at the spinal level:
questions.explanation: The cremasteric reflex tests the genitofemoral nerve (L1-L2).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The patellar tendon reflex is mediated at the spinal level:
questions.explanation: The knee jerk tests the femoral nerve (L2-L4).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The triceps tendon reflex is mediated at the spinal level:
questions.explanation: The triceps reflex tests the radial nerve (C7).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The Achilles tendon reflex is mediated at the spinal level:
questions.explanation: The ankle jerk tests the tibial nerve (S1).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: On the 0 to 4+ reflex scale, a brisk (full but exaggerated) response is graded:
questions.explanation: 3+ is brisker than average and possibly pathological.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: On the 0 to 4+ reflex scale, a normal reflex is graded:
questions.explanation: 2+ is a normal tendon reflex.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: On the 0 to 4+ reflex scale, a diminished reflex is graded:
questions.explanation: 1+ is a hypoactive reflex.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: On the 0 to 4+ reflex scale, a very brisk reflex with clonus is graded:
questions.explanation: 4+ is hyperactive with sustained clonus.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In the upper motor neuron lesion pattern, spasticity is more pronounced in the:

options.A: Upper limb flexors and lower limb extensors
options.B: Upper limb and lower limb extensors
options.C: Upper limb and lower limb flexors
options.D: Upper limb extensors and lower limb flexors

questions.explanation: Hemiplegic posture is flexion of the arm and extension of the leg.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The strongest component of the flexor synergy of the upper limb after stroke is:
questions.explanation: Elbow flexion is the strongest and the most easily elicited part of the flexor synergy.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The strongest component of the extensor synergy of the upper limb after stroke is:
questions.explanation: Pectoralis major produces strong shoulder adduction in the extensor synergy.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a component of the flexor synergy of the upper limb?
questions.explanation: The flexor synergy has scapular retraction/elevation, shoulder abduction and external rotation, elbow flexion and forearm supination.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a component of the extensor synergy of the upper limb?
questions.explanation: The extensor synergy has shoulder adduction and internal rotation, elbow extension and pronation.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a component of the flexor synergy of the lower limb?
questions.explanation: The lower limb flexor synergy is hip flexion, abduction, external rotation, knee flexion and ankle dorsiflexion.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a component of the extensor synergy of the lower limb?
questions.explanation: The lower limb extensor synergy is hip extension, adduction, internal rotation, knee extension and plantar flexion.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Resting (pill-rolling) tremors are typical of:
questions.explanation: A 4-6 Hz pill-rolling resting tremor is the hallmark tremor of Parkinson's disease.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Postural tremor is typically seen in:
questions.explanation: Fine postural tremors occur in hyperthyroidism and physiological tremor.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Intention tremor is typically seen in:
questions.explanation: Intention tremor increases as the limb approaches a target.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Tics are characteristic of:
questions.explanation: Tourette's syndrome features motor and vocal tics.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Chorea (fidgety, dance-like movements) is characteristic of:
questions.explanation: Huntington's disease affects the caudate nucleus with chorea and dementia.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In the Clinical Test of Sensory Interaction in Balance (CTSIB), a patient dependent on vision for sensory organisation will sway most in conditions:
questions.explanation: With the eyes closed or visual conflict on a firm surface, a visually dependent patient loses stability.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In the CTSIB, a patient dependent on somatosensory inputs will sway most in condition:
questions.explanation: Standing on foam with eyes open (condition 4) removes accurate somatosensory input.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In the CTSIB, a patient dependent on vestibular inputs will sway most in conditions:
questions.explanation: With eyes closed or visual conflict on foam, only the vestibular system is available.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The maximum score on the Berg Balance Scale is:
questions.explanation: The BBS has 14 items scored 0-4, total 56.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A Berg Balance Scale score of less than ______ is associated with a risk of falls.
questions.explanation: A score below 45 indicates increased risk of falling.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The standard functional reach for adults aged 20-40 years is about:
questions.explanation: Duncan's norms: 20-40 years about 14.5-17 inches.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The standard functional reach for adults aged 41-69 years is about:
questions.explanation: Functional reach declines with age.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The standard functional reach for adults aged 70-87 years is about:
questions.explanation: Reach of under about 6 inches indicates a high risk of falling.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In the Timed Up and Go test, a time of 10 seconds or less is considered:
questions.explanation: Healthy adults complete the TUG in 10 seconds or less.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In the Timed Up and Go test, a time of more than 30 seconds indicates:

options.B: High risk of falls and dependence on mobility aids

questions.explanation: A TUG over 30 seconds suggests dependency and a high fall risk.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The maximum score on the Performance Oriented Mobility Assessment (Tinetti POMA) is:
questions.explanation: The POMA has balance (16) and gait (12) sections.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A POMA score of less than 19 indicates:
questions.explanation: 19-24 is moderate fall risk; below 19 is high.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The Barthel Index total of 20 is converted to a 100-point score by multiplying by:
questions.explanation: Original 20-point Barthel score multiplied by 5 gives a 100-point score.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A Barthel score of 0-20 indicates:
questions.explanation: 0-20 total, 21-60 severe, 61-90 moderate, 91-99 slight dependency.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A Barthel score of 21-60 indicates:
questions.explanation: Scores of 21-60 indicate severe dependency.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A Barthel score of 61-90 indicates:
questions.explanation: Scores of 61-90 indicate moderate dependency.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A Barthel score of 91-99 indicates:
questions.explanation: Scores of 91-99 indicate slight dependency.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A lumbar puncture is performed at or below the level of:
questions.explanation: A needle is placed below the conus medullaris, usually in the L3-L4 or L4-L5 interspace.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The upper extremity is more affected in a stroke of the ______ artery.
questions.explanation: MCA strokes produce contralateral face and arm weakness more than leg weakness.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a primary (major) risk factor for stroke?
questions.explanation: Hypertension, smoking and diabetes are major modifiable factors.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a secondary risk factor for stroke?
questions.explanation: Hypertension is a primary risk factor; obesity, hyperlipidaemia and alcohol are secondary.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Trendelenburg gait results from weakness of the:
questions.explanation: Gluteus medius weakness lets the pelvis drop on the swing side.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Scissoring gait results from:
questions.explanation: Adductor spasticity (cerebral palsy) crosses the legs during swing.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Circumduction gait is due to:

options.A: Weak hip flexors (with spastic extensors) requiring a swing around the stiff leg

questions.explanation: The stiff leg is swung in a semicircle to clear the ground.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Knee locking (a stiff knee in stance) in gait is seen with:
questions.explanation: Quadriceps spasticity blocks knee flexion.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A hyperextended (recurvatum) knee during stance suggests:
questions.explanation: Patients with a weak quadriceps lock the knee back to stand.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In mild traumatic brain injury the post-traumatic amnesia lasts:

options.D: More than 24 hours but less than a week

questions.explanation: Mild TBI: PTA under 24 hours.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In moderate traumatic brain injury the post-traumatic amnesia lasts:

options.B: More than 24 hours but less than a week

questions.explanation: Moderate TBI: PTA of 1-7 days.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In severe traumatic brain injury the post-traumatic amnesia lasts:

options.D: More than 24 hours but less than a week

questions.explanation: Severe TBI: PTA of more than 7 days.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Restoration of normal motor function is stage ______ in Brunnstrom's stages of recovery.
questions.explanation: Brunnstrom stage 7 is normal function.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Spasticity begins to decline at Brunnstrom stage:
questions.explanation: Stage 3 is peak spasticity; it begins to decrease at stage 4.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Spasticity first appears at Brunnstrom stage:
questions.explanation: Stage 1 is flaccidity; spasticity and minimal synergies appear at stage 2.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Coordinated, isolated joint movements are seen at Brunnstrom stage:
questions.explanation: Stage 6 has isolated joint movements and near-normal coordination.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: On the ASIA scale a complete spinal cord injury is graded:
questions.explanation: ASIA A is complete: no motor or sensory function in S4-S5.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: On the ASIA scale an incomplete injury in which only sensory function is preserved below the level is graded:
questions.explanation: ASIA B: sensory incomplete, no motor function.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: On the ASIA scale, an incomplete injury with motor function preserved but more than half of key muscles below the level graded less than 3 is:
questions.explanation: ASIA C: motor incomplete with most key muscles below grade 3.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: On the ASIA scale, an incomplete injury with at least half of the key muscles below the level having grade 3 or more is:
questions.explanation: ASIA D is a useful motor incomplete injury.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: On the ASIA scale, a patient with normal motor and sensory function is graded:
questions.explanation: ASIA E is normal.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Central cord syndrome is most often seen after a:

options.A: Hyperextension injury of the cervical spine

questions.explanation: Central cord syndrome follows hyperextension in a spondylotic neck, with arms weaker than legs.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Anterior cord syndrome is most often seen after a:
questions.explanation: Anterior cord syndrome follows flexion injuries or anterior spinal artery occlusion.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Flexion injuries of the cervical spinal cord most commonly occur at:
questions.explanation: Flexion injuries are commonest at the mobile C5-C6 segment.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Extension injuries of the cervical spinal cord most commonly occur at:
questions.explanation: Hyperextension injuries often affect C4-C5.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A wide-based, high steppage gait due to loss of proprioception is seen in:
questions.explanation: Posterior column loss produces sensory ataxia.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The upper extremity is more affected than the lower extremity in:
questions.explanation: Central cord syndrome gives disproportionate arm weakness.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In Brown-Sequard syndrome there is:

options.A: Contralateral loss of dorsal column functions and ipsilateral loss of spinothalamic functions
options.B: Ipsilateral loss of dorsal column functions and contralateral loss of spinothalamic functions
options.D: Loss of only spinothalamic functions bilaterally

questions.explanation: Hemisection causes ipsilateral motor and proprioceptive loss and contralateral pain and temperature loss.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Autonomic dysreflexia is seen when the spinal cord injury is at or above the level of:
questions.explanation: Autonomic dysreflexia occurs in injuries at T6 and above.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In the Hoehn and Yahr classification, stage 1 Parkinson's disease is:

options.A: Bilateral involvement with balance not affected
options.B: Severe disability needing assistance to walk

questions.explanation: Stage 1: unilateral signs only.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In the Hoehn and Yahr classification, stage 2 Parkinson's disease is:
questions.explanation: Stage 2: bilateral involvement, balance intact.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In the Hoehn and Yahr classification, stage 3 Parkinson's disease is characterised by:
questions.explanation: Stage 3: first stage with postural reflex impairment; mild to moderate disability.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In the Hoehn and Yahr classification, stage 4 Parkinson's disease is characterised by:

options.C: Severe disability; walking only with assistance

questions.explanation: Stage 4: severely disabling but still able to walk or stand unassisted.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In the Hoehn and Yahr classification, stage 5 Parkinson's disease is characterised by:
questions.explanation: Stage 5 is wheelchair-bound or bedridden unless aided.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following seizures involves no convulsions?
questions.explanation: Absence seizures cause brief loss of awareness without convulsive movements.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Clonic contractions that spread in an orderly (march-like) fashion along the body are known as:
questions.explanation: Jacksonian seizures are focal motor seizures with progressive spread (Jacksonian march).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The Dix-Hallpike test for BPPV is performed by:

options.A: Moving the patient from supine to sitting with neck flexion
options.B: Turning the head, then moving the patient from sitting to supine with the neck extended about 30 degrees
options.C: Rotating the head while the patient lies prone
options.D: Flexing the neck with the patient supine

questions.explanation: The head is turned 45 degrees and the patient is taken rapidly back with the head hanging 20-30 degrees below horizontal.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In neuropraxia:

options.B: The nerve is stretched with Wallerian degeneration
options.C: There is no damage to the axons, epineurium, perineurium or endoneurium
options.D: All components of the nerve are severed

questions.explanation: Neuropraxia is a conduction block with intact nerve structure and good recovery.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In axonotmesis:

options.A: The axons are damaged but the epineurium, perineurium and endoneurium are intact
options.C: All components of the nerve are severed

questions.explanation: Axonotmesis has Wallerian degeneration with recovery possible along intact sheaths.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In neurotmesis:

options.C: There is only a conduction block
options.D: All components of the nerve are severed

questions.explanation: Neurotmesis is complete transection and needs surgical repair.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following can trigger pain in trigeminal neuralgia (tic douloureux)?

options.A: Extremes of temperature, brushing the teeth and talking

questions.explanation: Light touch to trigger zones, chewing, talking and cold air provoke the stabbing pain.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In Bell's palsy the lesion lies in the facial nerve:
questions.explanation: A lower motor neuron facial palsy involves the whole face on one side.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In Bell's palsy, taste sensation is lost from the ______ of the tongue.
questions.explanation: The chorda tympani branch of the facial nerve carries taste from the anterior two-thirds.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Crocodile tears (lacrimation while eating) are often seen in paralysis of the ______ cranial nerve.
questions.explanation: Aberrant regeneration of facial parasympathetic fibres causes crocodile tears.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In Guillain-Barre syndrome, muscle weakness/paralysis progresses in which order?
questions.explanation: GBS typically begins distally in the legs and ascends.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Stage 1 of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis shows:
questions.explanation: In early ALS weakness is mild and patients are largely independent.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Independence in ambulation in ALS starts to be lost at stage:
questions.explanation: Ambulation independence is lost in the 4th stage in the book's staging.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is unaffected in post-polio syndrome?
questions.explanation: Post-polio syndrome causes new weakness, fatigue and pain but not new sensory loss.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In Adams' closed-loop theory, great importance is placed on:
questions.explanation: Adams' theory depends on feedback and the perceptual trace built by practice.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In Schmidt's schema (open-loop) theory, great importance is placed on:
questions.explanation: Variable practice develops generalised motor programs and schemas.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Repetitive practice of the same task is called:
questions.explanation: Blocked practice repeats one task before moving to the next.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Practice of tasks in a non-predictable order is:
questions.explanation: Random practice interleaves tasks unpredictably and improves retention.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Practice of tasks in a predictable order is:
questions.explanation: Serial practice repeats a fixed sequence of tasks.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Continuous practice with little rest time is:
questions.explanation: Massed practice has more practice time than rest.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Practice in which rest time is greater than practice time is:
questions.explanation: Distributed practice includes frequent rest periods.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Cognitive rehearsal of a task without physical movement is:
questions.explanation: Mental practice rehearses the movement mentally.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: When the patient is anxious, or when the cognitive component of a task is large, ______ practice is valuable.
questions.explanation: Mental practice reduces anxiety and rehearses cognitive elements.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: ______ practice will improve performance during early learning.
questions.explanation: Blocked practice improves immediate performance, while random practice improves retention and transfer.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In the cognitive stage of learning the learner focuses on:
questions.explanation: The cognitive stage involves understanding the task and its goal, with many errors.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In the associative stage of learning the learner focuses on:
questions.explanation: The associative stage refines the movement with fewer errors.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In the autonomous stage of learning the learner focuses on:
questions.explanation: The autonomous stage allows automatic performance with attention directed to the goal.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Abundant errors and high dependence on vision are characteristic of which stage of learning?
questions.explanation: Early learners make many errors and rely on visual feedback.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Error-free performance with environmental challenges is typical of which stage of learning?
questions.explanation: Skills are automatic and can be practised in changing environments.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Inconsistent performance with reduced errors is typical of which stage of learning?
questions.explanation: Performance improves but is still variable.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Sensory stimulation is of great use in which stage of learning?
questions.explanation: Extra sensory cues help the novice learner.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Training intensity is less in:
questions.explanation: Modified CIMT has shorter restraint time and lower intensity than the original CIMT.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The duration of CIMT is ______ weeks and that of modified CIMT is ______ weeks.
questions.explanation: Original CIMT is a 2-3 week intensive programme; modified CIMT extends over about 8 weeks.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following sensory stimuli is NOT facilitatory?
questions.explanation: Prolonged stretch and neutral warmth/cold are inhibitory; icing, quick stretch, tapping and approximation facilitate.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following sensory stimuli is NOT inhibitory?
questions.explanation: Light touch is facilitatory (superficial) while deep pressure, warmth and slow stroking are inhibitory.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: When the involved upper limb is raised above 100 degrees with the elbow extended and the fingers abduct and extend, the phenomenon is known as:
questions.explanation: Soques' phenomenon is an associated reaction of finger extension on raising the arm.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: When the affected lower extremity abducts or adducts if abduction or adduction is resisted in the sound limb, the phenomenon is known as:
questions.explanation: Raimiste's phenomenon is a contralateral associated reaction in the hemiplegic leg.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Declarative learning can be improved by:
questions.explanation: Declarative (explicit) learning depends on attention and conscious processing.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: For a patient with a C6 level spinal cord injury the most appropriate wheelchair is:

options.A: Manual wheelchair with standard hand rims
options.D: Manual wheelchair with friction hand rims

questions.explanation: A C6 patient can propel with friction (coated) rims; C1-C5 need power chairs.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: For a patient with a high (C1-C5) cervical lesion the most appropriate wheelchair is:
questions.explanation: Elbow flexors and shoulder muscles are insufficient for manual propulsion.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: For an autonomous bladder, the Crede manoeuvre is indicated if the residual urine after voiding is:
questions.explanation: Crede (suprapubic pressure) is appropriate when residual urine is low; otherwise catheterisation is needed.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is TRUE for treadmill training in spinal cord injury?

options.A: It is only for complete injuries
options.B: It needs no body weight support
options.C: It is limited to 5 minutes a day
options.D: It should be given in incomplete injuries and not in complete spinal injuries; about 4 days/week for 8-12 weeks, 20-30 minutes

questions.explanation: Body-weight supported treadmill training is intended for motor-incomplete injuries.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following statements is FALSE with respect to neurological changes seen with ageing?

options.C: There is loss of cells in the cerebral cortex
options.D: There is lipofuscin and neurofibrillary tangle deposition

questions.explanation: The ventricles dilate (not constrict) as brain tissue atrophies.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following statements is TRUE with respect to neurological changes seen with ageing?

options.A: Reaction time increases and movement time decreases
options.B: Reaction time decreases and movement time increases
options.D: Both reaction time and movement time increase

questions.explanation: Slowed conduction and processing lengthen reaction and movement times.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: With ageing, the vibratory sensibility threshold increase is:

options.D: Greater in the lower extremity than the upper extremity

questions.explanation: Distal and lower limb vibration sense declines first.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: With ageing, impairment of memory is seen mainly in:

options.C: Short-term memory, with long-term memory retained

questions.explanation: Recent memory is affected more than remote memory.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The following are principles of motor development EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Development proceeds from stability to mobility, not the reverse.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal age of response of the asymmetrical tonic neck reflex (ATNR) is:
questions.explanation: The ATNR is present from birth and integrated by about 4-6 months.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal age of response of the tonic labyrinthine reflex (TLR) is:
questions.explanation: The TLR is a primitive reflex integrated by about 6 months.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal age of response of the palmar grasp reflex is:
questions.explanation: The palmar grasp is replaced by voluntary grasp by about 4-6 months.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The rooting reflex is normally present until about:
questions.explanation: The rooting reflex fades by about 3-4 months.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal age of response of the Moro reflex is until about:
questions.explanation: The Moro reflex disappears by 4-6 months; persistence suggests neurological dysfunction.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The stepping (walking) reflex is normally present until about:
questions.explanation: The newborn stepping reflex disappears by about 2 months.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal age of response of the Landau reflex is:
questions.explanation: The Landau reaction appears at about 4 months and is integrated by 12-24 months.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal age of response of the optical and labyrinthine righting reactions is:
questions.explanation: Head-righting reactions appear in early infancy and persist throughout life.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: An infant who shows no head lag when pulled to sit is usually at the age of:
questions.explanation: Head control in the pull-to-sit test is complete by about 4 months.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Independent sitting develops at about:
questions.explanation: Most infants sit without support at about 6-7 months.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The fine pincer grasp develops at about:
questions.explanation: Neat pincer grasp (thumb and index tip) appears at about 9-12 months.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Independent walking develops at about:
questions.explanation: Most children walk alone at about 12-15 months.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: According to the tonic labyrinthine reflex (TLR), prone position increases ______ tone and supine position increases ______ tone.
questions.explanation: TLR: prone increases flexor tone; supine increases extensor tone.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In the Galant reflex, stroking the spine from the shoulder toward the hip causes the trunk to:

options.B: Laterally flex on the opposite side
options.C: Extend on the side of the stimulus
options.D: Laterally flex on the side of the stimulus

questions.explanation: Galant (trunk incurvation) bends the trunk toward the stimulated side.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: According to the symmetrical tonic neck reflex (STNR), when the head is flexed the arms ______ and the legs ______.
questions.explanation: Neck flexion increases arm flexion and leg extension.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: According to the symmetrical tonic neck reflex (STNR), when the head is extended the arms ______ and the legs ______.
questions.explanation: Neck extension increases arm extension and leg flexion.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: According to the asymmetrical tonic neck reflex (ATNR), when the head is turned to one side the face-side extremities ______ and the skull-side extremities ______.
questions.explanation: The ATNR gives the 'fencer' posture: face-side extension and skull-side flexion.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In prematurity, the following is advisable EXCEPT:

options.B: Use of infant walkers and jumpers

questions.explanation: Walkers and jumpers encourage abnormal tone and delayed motor skills in premature infants.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A lesion of the cerebellum results in:
questions.explanation: Cerebellar involvement causes ataxic CP with poor balance and coordination.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The following helps in decreasing extensor tone EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Supine lying increases extensor tone through the tonic labyrinthine reflex.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Herniation of the cord and meninges through the vertebral defect is seen in:
questions.explanation: Myelomeningocele contains neural tissue in the sac.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following muscles is NOT involved in Erb's palsy?
questions.explanation: Erb's palsy affects the C5-C6 muscles; the hand intrinsics (C8-T1) are spared.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following muscles is involved in Klumpke's palsy?
questions.explanation: Klumpke's palsy involves C8-T1 and the small muscles of the hand.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The level of involvement in Erb's palsy is:
questions.explanation: Erb-Duchenne palsy affects the upper trunk (C5-C6).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The level of involvement in Klumpke's palsy is:
questions.explanation: Klumpke's palsy affects the lower trunk (C8-T1).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Hip flexor weakness is expected when the level of spina bifida involvement is:
questions.explanation: Hip flexors (L1-L2) are affected in upper lumbar lesions.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Hip adductor and knee extensor weakness is expected when the level of spina bifida involvement is:
questions.explanation: L2-L4 supply the adductors and quadriceps.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Hip abductor, knee flexor and dorsiflexor weakness is expected when the level of spina bifida involvement is:
questions.explanation: L4-L5 supply gluteus medius, hamstrings and tibialis anterior.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Weakness of the ankle plantar flexors is expected when the level of spina bifida involvement is:
questions.explanation: The calf muscles are supplied by S1-S2.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The following statement is true for Down's syndrome EXCEPT:

options.A: There is increased tone of muscles
options.B: Laxity of the atlantoaxial ligament can result in atlantoaxial subluxation
options.C: It is also known as trisomy 21
options.D: There are associated impairments in vision and hearing

questions.explanation: Down syndrome shows hypotonia, not increased tone.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT true for Duchenne muscular dystrophy?

options.B: Progressive weakness from distal to proximal
options.C: Absence of the dystrophin gene product

questions.explanation: DMD weakness begins in the proximal (pelvic girdle) muscles and progresses distally.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Acute infantile spinal muscular atrophy is also called:
questions.explanation: SMA type 1 presents before 6 months and is the severe infantile form.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Juvenile spinal muscular atrophy is also called:
questions.explanation: SMA type 3 begins after 18 months and has the mildest course.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Chronic childhood spinal muscular atrophy is:
questions.explanation: SMA type 2 presents between 6 and 18 months; children can sit but not walk.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: With a high-level lumbar spina bifida lesion, ambulation is possible with:
questions.explanation: High lesions need hip control, provided by an RGO or HKAFO.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: If the spina bifida level of involvement is lumbosacral, the ambulation orthosis prescribed is:
questions.explanation: With intact hip and knee control, an AFO is sufficient.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The function of an adductor pad (abduction wedge) in cerebral palsy is to:
questions.explanation: A pad between the thighs keeps the hips abducted.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The function of scooter boards in paediatric rehabilitation is to:

options.B: Facilitate hand movement in the visual field

questions.explanation: Prone scooting strengthens the neck and trunk extensors and the upper limbs.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Standers are used in children primarily to:

options.A: Promote hand movement in the visual field
options.D: Facilitate acetabulum formation and bone loading

questions.explanation: Standing in weight bearing promotes hip development, bone density and alignment.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Swings are used in paediatric therapy mainly to help:
questions.explanation: Vestibular input from swinging aids sensory integration.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Side lyers (side-lying boards) facilitate:

options.C: Movement of the hand within the visual field

questions.explanation: Side lying keeps the hands in midline and in the child's visual field.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT true for the Pavlik harness?

options.A: It is used in congenital hip dysplasia
options.B: It helps contain the femoral head in the acetabulum
options.C: The hips are positioned in flexion and adduction
options.D: The hips are positioned in flexion and abduction

questions.explanation: The Pavlik harness holds the hips flexed and abducted, not adducted.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Failure of integration of the ATNR interferes with:
questions.explanation: ATNR persistence blocks midline hand use, feeding and rolling.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Failure of integration of the STNR interferes with:
questions.explanation: STNR persistence causes 'bunny hopping' instead of reciprocal crawling.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Failure of integration of the TLR interferes with:
questions.explanation: TLR persistence prevents rolling and head lifting against gravity.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Failure of integration of the Galant reflex interferes with:

options.D: Development of sitting balance and can result in scoliosis

questions.explanation: A persistent Galant reflex causes trunk curvature and asymmetrical sitting.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Failure of integration of the palmar grasp reflex interferes with:
questions.explanation: Retained palmar grasp prevents voluntary release.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Failure of integration of the plantar grasp reflex interferes with:

options.A: Ability to stand on a flat surface

questions.explanation: Retained plantar grasp curls the toes and disturbs standing and walking.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Failure of integration of the rooting reflex interferes with:
questions.explanation: Rooting persistence disturbs feeding and oral control.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Failure of integration of the Moro reflex interferes with:
questions.explanation: A retained Moro reflex disturbs protective extension and sitting balance.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Failure of integration of the startle reflex interferes with:
questions.explanation: A retained startle reflex causes hypersensitivity and poor social engagement.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Failure of integration of the positive support reflex interferes with:
questions.explanation: A persistent positive support reflex produces stiff extension and prevents stepping.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The plantar grasp reflex is normally present until about:
questions.explanation: The plantar grasp disappears by about 9-10 months, before walking.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The positive support reflex is normally present until about:
questions.explanation: It fades by about 2 months and returns voluntarily with standing.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The Galant reflex is normally present until about:
questions.explanation: The Galant reflex usually disappears by 2-3 months.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The startle reflex is normally present until about:
questions.explanation: The startle reflex is integrated by about 4-5 months.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which transfer technique is used when a patient has an incomplete spinal cord injury with enough lower limb strength?
questions.explanation: Patients with preserved lower limb function can bear weight in a stand-pivot transfer.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which transfer technique is used when a patient has a complete spinal cord injury at C5-C6 level?
questions.explanation: C5-C6 patients usually need a sliding board with assistance.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
